# English abstract {.unnumbered}

Despite operational settings of the FSSG throughout the experiments of 2024 being fixed, passage efficiency varied substantially as it ranged between 0.47 and 0.79. It is very difficult to determine the underlying cause behind this difference as these passage efficiency values are not exact values but underestimations and local, potentially interfering, conditions might have been present but were only sporadically measured (e.g. water quality). In addition, fish were re-used for the different experiments and their familiarity with the system might have had an effect (though the available results do not indicate any effect). The length, weight and species did not have any effect on whether fish were able to successfully use the fish spiral, nor did it have an effect on the time it took fish to move up the fish spiral. Only a limited number of fish went through the FSSG multiple times. Fish generally wait until the valves are completely open before entering and leaving the fish spiral, though for the upper valve a relatively large amount of fish also seem to leave the fish spiral when the valve is opening or closing.
